title: chats-merge — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins the conversation merge rules in myne-core (merge_chats_catalog + merge_chats_turns, myne-md/myne#675; sync-protocol.md §11.4 + §10.2.5). Pure logic over decoded plaintexts — no keys, no AEAD. Catalog entries are roster rows {created_at,deleted_at?,title,updated_at,version?} keyed by conversation-id hex; turn lists are turn-id string arrays. Four case kinds: 'catalog_merge' (two-sided join; the runner asserts BOTH argument orders, so commutativity is structural), 'catalog_merge_assoc' (three-sided join; the runner asserts (A+B)+C equals A+(B+C)), 'turns_merge' (two-sided join, both orders asserted), 'turns_merge_content' (one turn id held by both sides; the monotone decision marker is reconciled, both orders asserted). The remove-wins tombstone tie and the wholesale enrollment seed are catalog_merge cases. The Rust reference implementation lives at core/src/plugins/sync/conflict.rs (main myne repository).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'chats-merge/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

oneOf.title: catalog_merge — pin a two-sided roster join

input_local.description: One side's roster: conversation-id hex -> roster row.

expected_merged.description: The join both argument orders must produce: per-key higher version wins, equal-version ties resolve remove-wins (a tombstone outranks a live row), disjoint keys union.

oneOf.title: catalog_merge_assoc — pin a three-sided roster join

expected_merged.description: The join both groupings must produce: (A+B)+C equals A+(B+C).

oneOf.title: turns_merge — pin a two-sided turn-list join

input_local.description: One side's turn-id list (turn ids embed a client discriminator, e.g. <boot>-<seq>).

expected_merged.description: The join both argument orders must produce: the common prefix verbatim once, then both divergent suffixes in turn-id order; an id on both sides contributes once.

oneOf.title: turns_merge_content — pin one turn's content merge

input_local.description: One side's turn object for the same turn id.

input_remote.description: The other side's turn object, same id.

expected_merged.description: The merge both argument orders must produce. The decided set is closed (applied|rejected); an unknown value counts as undecided; two disagreeing decisions resolve by a fixed order on the value (applied before rejected); the marker is grafted onto the local turn, so a field only one side carries is preserved. Both sides of a case therefore carry the same other fields.
